method.value: Stack LMC stars in three detector-position bins; insert empirical PSFs into MIDIS calibrated exposures and difference resampled runs with and without inserted stars.

evidence.quote: Instead, we create the empirical PSFs by stacking stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) images from the commissioning program ID 1473 and two calibration programs (IDs: 1040 and 1024).
The images are resampled keeping the native detector orientation, which enables us to separately stack three bins of stars, situated in upper, middle, and lower detector positions.
We then run the Stage 3 Imaging Processing twice, once with the inserted stars and once without, and recover the varying PSF model by taking the difference.

These wavelengths trace the bulk of the (older) stellar light, that remained inaccessible with HST, and are less affected by dust attenuation than observations at shorter wavelengths.

why_this_method.value: Empirical position-dependent PSFs address MIRI detector diffraction; established HST fits avoid uncertain NIRCam PSFs.

evidence.quote: The shape of the cruciform artefact is dependent on the angle of incidence and varies with position across the detector, with the spikes effectively bending inwards towards the center of the detector.
For these reasons, we construct a varying PSF model for the MIDIS field making use of empirical PSFs at different positions on the MIRI detector.

referee_caveats_inferred: The results section reports 35% smaller ASPECS sizes at 1 < z < 2, whereas the conclusions give a size ratio ≈0.75 near z ≈1.5; these are inconsistent and require clarification.
Near-infrared light is used as a proxy for stellar-mass structure without resolved mass-map fitting.
No numerical correlation coefficients, fitted slopes or significance levels are supplied for the mass-related trends.
Similarity to the reference population is asserted without a stated quantitative distribution-comparison test.
Per-source manual neighbor adjustments and mask edits limit exact automation.
ALMA mainly supplies selection and existing photometry here; the paper does not provide an ALMA visibility-reduction recipe.

data_public_as_stated.value: JWST/NIRCam HUDF imaging is publicly available; ALMA public status not stated.

The observations can be accessed via <http://dx.doi.org/10.17909/gn5v-f189>.
